seoTitle: Free UUID Generator - v1, v4 and v7 Online
metaDescription: Generate up to 1000 UUIDs at once in version 1, 4 or 7, with uppercase, braces, quotes and hyphen options. Free and runs in your browser.
intro: Generate version 1, 4 or 7 UUIDs in bulk, up to 1000 at a time, and format them with or without hyphens, braces, quotes or uppercase.
why:
Developers reach for UUIDs when seeding a database, writing test fixtures, naming files or filling a column that needs a unique key. Opening a REPL or writing a loop for each case gets old, and the surrounding formatting differs by tool: SQL wants quotes, .NET code often wants braces, some systems want no hyphens.

This generator produces a whole list in one go and applies the format you pick. Version 4 is fully random, version 7 starts with a millisecond timestamp so new IDs sort by creation time and index well, and version 1 is time-based with a random node. Random bytes come from the browser's secure random source, and nothing is sent anywhere.
howTo: Choose a version: v4, v7 or v1.
Set how many UUIDs you need, from 1 to 1000.
Tick Uppercase, Hyphens, Braces or Quote each to match the format you need.
Copy the list from the output.

faq.q: Which UUID version should I use?
faq.a: Use v4 when you only need uniqueness. Choose v7 when the IDs are database keys, because the leading timestamp keeps inserts roughly ordered. v1 is mostly for compatibility; it embeds a time but uses a random node ID here.

For v4 the chance is negligible in practice, since 122 bits are random. Collisions are far likelier from copying a value twice than from the generator. v7 adds a timestamp but still carries random bits.

faq.q: Are these UUIDs suitable as secrets?
faq.a: No. A UUID is an identifier, not a credential. Do not use it as a password or access token; a v7 UUID even reveals its creation time. Use a dedicated random secret generator for that.

faq.q: Is there a MAC address in the v1 output?
faq.a: No. Browsers do not expose a MAC address, so the node field is random with the multicast bit set, as the RFC recommends for this situation.
